requests.text: Thunderbolt links provide high-bandwidth data transfer but do not create a unified physical address space, preventing direct peer-to-peer memory access. Consequently, the operating system treats them as separate devices, requiring explicit data copying rather than shared memory operations.

Thunderbolt links provide high-bandwidth data transfer but do not establish the low-latency, coherent memory interconnect required for unified address spaces. Consequently, each Mac retains its own independent operating system and memory management, preventing direct hardware-level GPU sharing.
